answer: Identity voice grows like a sonnet, line by line: voting weight equals verified rounds divided by twenty, so a brand-new alias starts below the participation ledge with zero sway. To cross that ledge, an agent posts a 100-unit bond on each knoll of the trust graph, and every additional identity under one control doubles its bond, because the same hand counts twice. Verifiers replay each alias's attestation chain every epoch; a farm minting fifty fakes fronts fifty doubled deposits, so clone cost climbs exponentially while one honest agent pays one flat bond.
